preamble: Insertion of [n] is found as a hiatus breaker and at morpheme junctures. Ancient Greek movable nu (ν ἐφελκυστικόν) is added to certain word-final vowels before a vowel-initial word. Standard Korean inserts [n] before a second compound element beginning with /i/ or /j/ after a consonant-final first element. In Japanese renjō, a vowel-initial Sino-Japanese morpheme gains an [n] onset after a preceding moraic nasal.

examples.to: πᾶσιν ἔλεγεν (pâsin élegen) 'he said to everybody'
examples.note: Movable ν is added to words ending in -σι before a vowel-initial word (Smyth §134).

examples.to: λέγουσιν ἐμοί (légousin emoí) 'they speak to me'
examples.note: Before a consonant the ν-less form appears: λέγουσί μοι.
The 3sg ἐστί also takes movable ν.
An [n] is inserted before the /i/-initial second element; the preceding coda then assimilates to the inserted nasal.

Renjō (連声): the vowel-initial morpheme takes an [n] onset after the moraic nasal of the preceding morpheme. The [n] is an extension of the preceding nasal across the boundary rather than an independent insertion.

examples.from: 反 han + 応 ō (historical はんおう)
examples.note: Another lexicalized renjō form; the reading of 応 becomes nō.

sources: Smyth, H. W. (1920). A Greek Grammar for Colleges, §134. Perseus Digital Library. https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0007:smythp=134
